title: Foundry tracing and Application Insights
summary: Foundry can collect traces for its agents server-side after you connect an Application Insights resource to the project, with no code change. Client-side tracing and the Agents view add depth, and KQL over the dependencies table answers custom questions.
useIf: Your agents run in Foundry Agent Service, or you want one Application Insights resource to hold traces from Foundry and your own code.
avoidIf: You assume server-side tracing covers every agent type, or that Foundry traces and Agent Framework telemetry are the same pipeline.

explain.md: **Server-side tracing** turns on after you connect an Application Insights resource to the Foundry project. No code change is needed. It is generally available for prompt and hosted agents and in preview for workflow and external agents. Foundry stores traces in Application Insights using the OTel GenAI conventions, and the portal Traces tab shows 90 days. You need the Log Analytics Reader role, plus Privileged Monitoring Data Reader if the tables are protected [[r12]].

**Client-side tracing** (preview) instruments your own code that talks to Foundry. Set `AZURE_EXPERIMENTAL_ENABLE_GENAI_TRACING=true` (Python) or `AppContext.SetSwitch("Azure.Experimental.EnableGenAITracing", true)` (.NET) before creating the client. Traces typically appear within a few minutes (2 to 5 minutes on the client-side page). Message content recording uses `OTEL_INSTRUMENTATION_GENAI_CAPTURE_MESSAGE_CONTENT=true`, and `@trace_function` records parameters and return values regardless [[r12]] [[r13]].

explain.md: In Application Insights the **Agents (Preview)** blade is built on the OTel GenAI semantics. It shows agent runs, tool calls, models and GenAI errors, can sort traces by tokens used, and offers prebuilt Grafana dashboards for Agent Framework, Agent Framework workflows, Foundry and coding agents. It relies on `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens` and `gen_ai.usage.output_tokens`. Spans land in the `dependencies` table with attributes in `customDimensions` [[r14]].

explain.title: Confirm gen_ai attributes reach Application Insights (Microsoft Learn query)
explain.code:
dependencies
| where timestamp > ago(1h)
| where customDimensions has "gen_ai.agent.name"
| project timestamp, name, customDimensions
| take 20

explain.title: Tokens per agent (composed from documented attribute names, verify against your data)
explain.code:
dependencies
| where timestamp > ago(1d)
| where customDimensions has "gen_ai.usage.input_tokens"
| extend agent = tostring(customDimensions["gen_ai.agent.name"]),
         inTok = toint(customDimensions["gen_ai.usage.input_tokens"]),
         outTok = toint(customDimensions["gen_ai.usage.output_tokens"])
| summarize calls = sum(itemCount), inputTokens = sum(inTok * itemCount), outputTokens = sum(outTok * itemCount) by agent
| order by outputTokens desc

pitfalls.symptom: No traces appear in the Foundry Traces tab
pitfalls.cause: No Application Insights resource is connected to the project, or the reader lacks Log Analytics Reader
pitfalls.fix: Connect the resource, grant Log Analytics Reader (and Privileged Monitoring Data Reader for protected tables) and wait a few minutes [[r12]]

pitfalls.cause: The experimental tracing switch was set after the client was created, or not at all
pitfalls.fix: Set `AZURE_EXPERIMENTAL_ENABLE_GENAI_TRACING` or the .NET switch before creating the client [[r13]]

pitfalls.symptom: Agents view panels are empty although traces exist
pitfalls.cause: Spans lack `gen_ai.usage.input_tokens` and `gen_ai.usage.output_tokens`, which the view relies on
pitfalls.fix: Run the verification query and add or map the missing attributes [[r14]]

scenarios.title: Prompt agents in Foundry, compliance wants traces, no code changes
scenarios.situation: A team runs several prompt agents in Foundry Agent Service. Compliance wants traces for investigations. The team has no appetite for instrumenting code.
unknowns: Who needs read access to the data?
scenarios.question: How do you get traces?

options.name: Connect Application Insights to the Foundry project and enable server-side tracing, content recording off
options.why: GA for prompt agents, no code change and the Traces tab and Agents view work out of the box.
options.tradeoff: Tied to Application Insights, and content stays out of traces.

options.name: Wrap every agent call in custom client tracing
options.why: Adds your own spans and context.
options.tradeoff: Client-side tracing is preview and duplicates what the platform emits.

options.name: Log requests and responses in an app database
options.why: It stores content in a bespoke store without run structure.
options.tradeoff: Right if auditors require conversation records as a separate system.

flips.if: Agents are workflow or external agents
flips.then: Expect preview behavior and add client-side tracing.

flips.if: Content must be readable for audits
flips.then: Use a governed content store, not trace attributes.

scenarios.takeaway: Platform-hosted agents get platform tracing for free.

scenarios.title: Foundry agents plus self-hosted orchestration code
scenarios.situation: An orchestrator runs on containers and calls both Foundry agents and a partner agent. The team wants one trace view and one place for KQL.
unknowns: Is the exporter configured in the orchestrator?
scenarios.question: What setup do you choose?

options.name: Server-side tracing for Foundry agents plus OpenTelemetry in the orchestrator exporting to the same Application Insights
options.why: Each part is traced by the layer that owns it and everything lands in one store.
options.tradeoff: Two pipelines to configure and a preview client-side path.

options.name: Only server-side tracing
options.why: It misses your orchestrator and the partner hop.
options.tradeoff: Enough when every agent is hosted in Foundry.

options.name: Only client-side tracing
options.why: Covers your code and what you call.
options.tradeoff: Misses server-side internals of Foundry agents.

flips.if: Foundry agents are only prompt agents
flips.then: Server-side tracing may be all you need.
Export OTLP from the orchestrator and keep Foundry traces for Foundry agents.

scenarios.takeaway: Combine server-side and client-side tracing when hosting is mixed.

quiz.q: What turns on Foundry server-side tracing for prompt agents?
options: Connecting an Application Insights resource to the Foundry project
quiz.explain: Server-side tracing needs only the Application Insights connection and no code change. `UseOpenTelemetry` and `ENABLE_SENSITIVE_DATA` belong to Agent Framework telemetry, and Aspire is a local viewer.

quiz.q: Foundry traces are missing. Which checks are sensible? Select all that apply.
options: An Application Insights resource is connected to the project
The reader holds Log Analytics Reader (and Privileged Monitoring Data Reader if tables are protected)
For client-side spans, the tracing switch was set before the client was created
The agent must be a Semantic Kernel plugin
quiz.explain: The connection, the reader roles and the client-side switch are the documented prerequisites. Semantic Kernel plugins are not a requirement.

flashcards.front: Which Foundry agent types have GA server-side tracing?
flashcards.back: Prompt and hosted agents. Workflow and external agents, and client-side tracing, are preview (checked 2026-10-13).

flashcards.front: How long does the Foundry portal Traces tab show data?
flashcards.back: 90 days. Backend retention follows your Application Insights settings.

flashcards.front: Where do GenAI spans land in Application Insights?
flashcards.back: In the `dependencies` table, with attributes in `customDimensions`.
